data.description:
## Description

**What**: Upgrade commands.* keys to multi-valued (semicolon `;` separator). Keys: commands.test_runner, commands.lint, commands.format, commands.format_check, commands.lint_ruff, commands.lint_mypy. Demonstrate polyglot iteration via Python+JS fixture end-to-end.
**Why**: Polyglot projects need separate runners per language; semicolon avoids collision with comma-bearing args (e.g., pytest `-k 'foo,bar'`).
**Scope**:
- IN: Parser updates for the listed keys (semicolon split, trailing-empty strip); polyglot Python+JS fixture with commands.test_runner=pytest;npm test; validate.sh --ci runs both runners and reports separately; exercise bounded to commands.test_runner and commands.lint per epic SC3.
- OUT: Multi-runner orchestration logic / per-axis precedence rules; fixture exercises for commands.format/format_check/lint_ruff/lint_mypy beyond retrofitting the parser.

## Done Definitions
- When complete, commands.* keys parse semicolon-separated lists with trailing-empty elements stripped ← Satisfies: SC3
- When complete, the polyglot Python+JS fixture runs `validate.sh --ci` with both pytest and npm test executing and reporting separately ← Satisfies: SC1, SC3
- When complete, the smoke run asserts the emitted stack array contains exactly the expected polyglot tag set per epic SC1 ← Satisfies: SC1
- When complete, unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic

## Considerations
- [Reliability] Trailing-empty list element strip — covered by tests
- [Maintainability] Document semicolon-separator decision and rationale in CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md v2

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a maintainer, commands.* config keys are multi-valued and exercised in a polyglot smoke run
